summary: This README describes Refero, a package of one design skill plus a read-only MCP connection that gives AI agents access to curated visual styles, 150,000+ real app screens and 6,000+ user flows. Its core idea is that research is mandatory before implementation: the agent researches styles, then real screens and flows, extracts concrete patterns and locks references before building. It bundles guidance on typography, color, spacing, motion, icons and copywriting, and checks substantial visual work against the chosen direction before handoff. For someone building a design system, it is a model of an evidence-first AI design workflow and of how to ship one skill across many AI hosts. Most of the file is install and packaging instructions rather than design guidance.
key_ideas: Make research a required step before any design implementation
Research visual styles first, then real screens and user flows only when the task needs them
Extract concrete patterns and lock the chosen references before building
Tie design decisions to evidence rather than generic AI defaults
Check substantial visual work against the selected direction before handing it off
Bundle craft guidance for typography, color, spacing, motion, icons and copywriting with the skill
Ship one canonical skill folder and per-host manifests that all point to the same MCP endpoint
Keep a skill's references folder beside its SKILL.md when installing manually
Validate a release for manifests, versions, links, package boundaries and secret leaks
